overall_summary: Bitcoin faces a heavy bearish tape as sticky inflation, a surging dollar, and rising yields keep December hike odds fully priced, while ETF outflows extend to a seventh day. The slide toward sixty-seven thousand with large liquidations looks more like a washout already in motion than a fresh catalyst. Miner relief and pockets of institutional buying offer only limited offset against the macro headwinds.
key_points: ETF outflows hit seventh straight day
Sticky PPI and hike bets pressure risk
Dollar and yields at multi-month highs
Mining difficulty cut aids miner relief

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $185M on Seventh Straight Outflow Day
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw another $185 million in net outflows on Friday, extending the streak to seven sessions, with BlackRock's IBIT alone accounting for most of it on an eleventh straight red day. Roughly $2.35 billion has left the products over two weeks as Bitcoin slid. Traders should care because ETF flows have been a key institutional demand signal, and sustained redemptions remove a major bid just as price tests multi-month lows.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure and thinner institutional support near current levels

items.title: Bitcoin Crashes Toward $67K With Hundreds of Millions Liquidated
items.summary: Bitcoin fell to its lowest levels since August around $67,000 amid a broader risk-off move, with crypto liquidations hitting $1.47 billion earlier and hundreds of millions more overnight, overwhelmingly long positions. Drivers include higher Fed hike odds, Nvidia turmoil, and capital rotating toward the Anthropic IPO. Traders need to watch because cascading liquidations can accelerate downside, but washed-out leverage often sets up for stabilization if spot demand returns.
items.impact: Near-term volatility and potential capitulation washout at support

items.title: Strategy Paper Losses Hit Nearly $7 Billion on Bitcoin Holdings
items.summary: Michael Saylor's Strategy now sits on roughly $6.85 to $7.2 billion in unrealized losses on its 850,364 Bitcoin after the price dropped below its $75,456 average cost basis. The firm recently added more coins near $79,000 and continues to hold rather than sell. This matters for traders as Strategy is the largest corporate holder, and large paper losses can pressure its stock and sentiment even if no coins hit the market.
items.impact: Negative sentiment spillover to crypto-linked equities and holders

items.title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Plunges 9.13 Percent, Biggest Cut Since June
items.summary: Bitcoin's mining difficulty adjusted downward by 9.13 percent to about 134.82 trillion at block 975,744, the sharpest drop since June after recent hashrate softness. This makes mining roughly 10 percent more profitable in Bitcoin terms for remaining operators. Traders should note it because lower difficulty can stabilize miner economics during price weakness and may reduce forced selling of newly mined coins.
items.impact: Improved miner margins and reduced sell pressure from hash rate exits

items.title: DOJ Wins Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion From North Korea Binance Hack
items.summary: The US Justice Department obtained court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance by North Korean hackers, part of over $2.7 billion already frozen from the roughly $6 billion October heist. Authorities also disrupted related FaceStealer infrastructure used in other thefts. This is relevant because large recoveries reduce circulating illicit supply and demonstrate improving on-chain tracing and exchange cooperation, which can support longer-term confidence.
items.impact: Positive for industry security narrative and potential supply reduction

items.title: JPMorgan Crypto-Linked Holdings Approach $1 Billion in Latest Filing
items.summary: JPMorgan's Q3 13F shows roughly $981 million across Bitcoin ETFs, Strategy shares, and Coinbase, likely topping $1 billion when including Robinhood and miner stakes. The bank increased its IBIT position and boosted Strategy holdings by 36 percent. Institutional accumulation by the largest US bank provides a counter-signal to recent ETF outflows and underscores ongoing traditional finance exposure even in a down market.

items.title: October PPI Rises 0.3% MoM, YoY Hits 6.5% Multi-Year High
items.summary: Wholesale prices rose less than expected at 0.3 percent month over month in October, matching core expectations, but the annual rate climbed to 6.5 percent, the highest since late 2022. Goods and transportation costs drove much of the pressure. This keeps the Federal Reserve on track for a December rate hike and shows inflation remains sticky well above the 2 percent target, which matters for crypto because higher-for-longer rates tighten liquidity and pressure risk assets.
items.impact: Reinforces December hike odds and higher real yields, weighing on Bitcoin

items.title: US Dollar Index Hits 19-Month High Near 103.4
items.summary: The DXY closed Friday at about 103.41, its strongest level since April 2025 and on track for the best weekly gain in two months. The move was powered by surging Treasury yields and firming bets on Federal Reserve tightening after hot inflation data. A stronger dollar typically drains global liquidity and makes dollar-denominated assets like Bitcoin less attractive to international buyers, so traders should watch for continued pressure on crypto.
items.impact: Strong USD headwind for risk assets and BTC

items.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Climbs Above 5.15% on Hike Bets
items.summary: The benchmark 10-year yield closed near 5.15 percent Friday after a sharp weekly rise of roughly 30 basis points, with the two-year also jumping sharply. Markets are fully pricing a 25 basis point Fed hike in December and assigning double-digit odds to a 50 basis point move. Higher yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and tighten financial conditions overall.
items.impact: Elevated yields compress risk appetite across markets

items.title: NY Fed's Williams: Inflation Far Too High, More Action Needed
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said inflation remains stubbornly elevated and the central bank still has work to do to return it to 2 percent on a sustained basis. He described the economy as strong and the labor market solid while stressing further policy actions over time. His comments add to the hawkish chorus this week and solidify expectations for additional rate increases, which is negative for crypto liquidity.
items.impact: Hawkish signal locks in tighter policy path

items.title: Fed's Jefferson: Inflation Trajectory Key for Policy Path
items.summary: Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said Friday that with growth and the labor market solid, the path of inflation is now the more important signal for monetary policy. He noted persistent price pressures in recent data and said further adjustments will depend on incoming trends and risks. This keeps the door open to additional hikes and underscores that the Fed remains focused on sticky inflation rather than cutting soon.
items.impact: Supports continued restrictive stance into December

items.title: Markets Fully Price December Fed Hike After Sticky Data
items.summary: Following the week's CPI and PPI prints plus multiple hawkish Fed speeches, futures fully price at least a 25 basis point rate increase at the December meeting, with roughly 10 to 15 percent odds of a 50 basis point move. Officials including Waller earlier flagged the possibility of a larger step if core inflation stayed hot. For crypto traders this means the near-term rate path is tilted higher, reducing the chance of easy liquidity anytime soon.
items.impact: Higher rates priced in reduce near-term upside for risk assets

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin Set Historic Trilateral Summit in China
items.summary: The White House confirmed that Presidents Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will hold their first-ever joint meeting next week on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Agenda items include nuclear arms reductions after New START expired and the Iran war, while Ukraine is deliberately kept off the table. For traders this is a major multipolar signal that could ease or reprice global risk depending on whether it produces any de-escalation or just more theater.
items.impact: Potential volatility in risk assets and oil on any signals of great-power deal-making or deadlock

items.title: Iran Claims Strike on US Radar in Bahrain; US Denies
items.summary: Iran’s IRGC said it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for a US strike on Iranian telecom infrastructure near Hormuz, marking the first such claim in months. US Central Command denied any damage and said it shot down two Iranian drones with no casualties. Combined with Trump’s statement that America no longer needs a deal with Iran, this keeps Gulf energy routes and oil prices under pressure.
items.impact: Elevates oil-risk premium and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: Trump Sidelines Vance, Declares No Iran Deal Needed
items.summary: President Trump pulled Vice President Vance off Iran negotiations and ordered him to focus on domestic corruption probes instead, stating the US already controls Iranian money and the Strait of Hormuz. This freezes diplomacy after midterms blamed the war for Republican losses and leaves a prolonged stalemate with ongoing shipping risks. Traders should watch for continued elevated diesel and war-risk insurance costs that feed into broader inflation and risk sentiment.
items.impact: Prolongs energy-market uncertainty and keeps geopolitical risk premium elevated

items.title: Europe Invited to Next Ukraine Peace Talks After Putin Meetings
items.summary: US envoys Kushner and Witkoff met Putin in Moscow then Zelensky in Dublin; both sides agreed Europe will join the next round of negotiations, with a major prisoner exchange also sealed. Putin remains firm on territorial demands and rejects foreign peacekeepers, while Zelensky welcomed the European seat but fighting and infrastructure strikes continue. Progress toward a broader table is mildly constructive for risk assets if it reduces the chance of endless war.
items.impact: Modest risk-on support if talks gain traction and reduce European energy and security fears

items.title: Ukrainian Drones Cripple Russian Missile Corvette in Baltic
items.summary: Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Russian Buyan-M class corvette Naro-Fominsk in the Gulf of Finland, leaving it unable to sail independently with crew casualties confirmed by Estonian officials. The hit came alongside attacks on the Ust-Luga oil terminal and marks the first such warship strike in Baltic civilian shipping lanes. It shows Kyiv’s reach into NATO’s backyard even as peace talks advance, keeping Russian energy and naval assets under threat.
items.impact: Adds tactical pressure on Russian logistics without immediate broad market shock

items.title: Turkey and Qatar Sign Mutual Defense Pact
items.summary: Presidents Erdogan and Emir Tamim signed a mutual defense agreement in Istanbul pledging a unified response to any attack on either country, plus expanded military exercises and industry ties. The deal comes amid Gulf insecurity from the Iran war and follows earlier pacts involving Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. It signals further regional hedging that could stabilize or complicate energy corridors and alliances traders track for Middle East risk.
items.impact: Minor realignment signal with limited near-term price impact unless tested by conflict
